coordinate_convention: 0-based pixel centers; x = column; y = row; array index is [y, x]. Sky conversions use the file WCS (astropy or gwcs) with that same 0-based origin.

flags.meaning: Pipeline bit recommending that the pixel be left out of science measurements, including when it is combined with other bits. It does not name a single physical cause.
flags.name: DO_NOT_USE

flags.meaning: The exposure-level saturation step recorded saturation. Saturated pixels can distort shape and brightness. The flag does not classify the candidate.
flags.name: SATURATED

flags.meaning: Ramp fitting recorded a jump. Jumps are associated with cosmic-ray hits and with other discontinuities. A jump flag does not prove that this candidate is a cosmic ray.
flags.name: JUMP_DET

flags.meaning: Data were marked lost in transmission.
flags.name: DROPOUT

flags.meaning: The pixel lies in a region affected by the guide-window readout. The handbook notes that this condition is one of those that may also set DO_NOT_USE.
flags.name: GW_AFFECTED_DATA

flags.meaning: High persistence was flagged (this bit was previously reserved).
flags.name: PERSISTENCE

flags.meaning: The pixel was flagged as below the A/D floor.
flags.name: AD_FLOOR

flags.meaning: Pixel DQ bit 7: flagged by outlier detection. This is not the GROUPDQ WFI18_TRANSIENT bit.
flags.name: OUTLIER

flags.meaning: The quoted uncertainty was flagged as unreliable.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_ERROR

flags.meaning: The pixel is not on the science portion of the detector.
flags.name: NON_SCIENCE

flags.meaning: Reference data marked the pixel dead.
flags.name: DEAD

flags.meaning: Reference data marked the pixel hot.
flags.name: HOT

flags.meaning: Reference data marked the pixel warm.
flags.name: WARM

flags.meaning: Reference data marked the pixel as low quantum efficiency.
flags.name: LOW_QE

flags.meaning: Reference data marked the pixel as a telegraph pixel.
flags.name: TELEGRAPH

flags.meaning: The pixel was marked highly nonlinear.
flags.name: NONLINEAR

flags.meaning: A reference pixel was marked unusable.
flags.name: BAD_REF_PIXEL

flags.meaning: A flat field could not be measured.
flags.name: NO_FLAT_FIELD

flags.meaning: A gain could not be measured.
flags.name: NO_GAIN_VALUE

flags.meaning: A linearity correction was not available.
flags.name: NO_LIN_CORR

flags.meaning: A saturation check was not available.
flags.name: NO_SAT_CHECK

flags.meaning: Bias variance was marked large.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_BIAS

flags.meaning: Dark variance was marked large.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_DARK

flags.meaning: Slope variance was marked large.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_SLOPE

flags.meaning: Flat variance was marked large.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_FLAT

flags.meaning: Reserved bit. No scientific meaning is assigned.
flags.name: RESERVED_5

flags.meaning: Reserved bit. No scientific meaning is assigned.
flags.name: RESERVED_6

flags.meaning: The pixel was marked sensitive to the reset anomaly.
flags.name: UNRELIABLE_RESET

flags.meaning: Reserved bit. No scientific meaning is assigned.
flags.name: RESERVED_7

flags.meaning: Catch-all bad-pixel bit. The specific cause is not in the flag name.
flags.name: OTHER_BAD_PIXEL

flags.meaning: The pixel is a reference pixel.
flags.name: REFERENCE_PIXEL

notes: Documented snapshot of roman_datamodels.dqflags.pixel from version 1.2.0, cross-checked with the romancal reference-file DQ table. Bit 14 is unassigned. RC, inverse-RC, and open-pixel families described in the Roman DQ handbook are not separate names in this enum.
Named flags were read from roman_datamodels.dqflags.pixel at runtime.

limitations: SYNTHETIC_TEST. Input arrays are a labelled fixture, not a Roman observation.
v0.1 does not compare multiple exposures and does not join an L3 context map to L2 inputs.
Units come from the synthetic file. They are not Roman-calibrated units.

reference_model.note: A synthetic Gaussian is never recorded as a Roman PSF.

units_note: Units come from the synthetic file. They are not Roman-calibrated units.
